header:
Date: 2025-08-05 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Horizon - Head of Platform), Jamal Reed (Horizon - ML Engineer), Sofia Kim (Horizon - Security)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection between hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Customer needs: multilingual support, long context (>64k tokens ideally), function/tool-calling for retrieval and actions, strict security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and cost/latency tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: send model comparison + pricing, schedule technical benchmark deep-dive.
topics: Open model comparisons (Llama-2 variants, Mistral, MPT, Falcon, etc.)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Latency vs cost and batching/quantization options
transcript:
00:00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Ravi our SE. Can you all quickly intro?
00:00:08 Lena: Hi, Lena Ortiz, head of platform at Horizon. We're evaluating inference vendors for our new assistant product.
00:00:12 Jamal: Jamal Reed, ML eng, I'll own the benchmarks.
00:00:15 Sofia: Sofia Kim, security and compliance.
00:00:18 Ravi: Quick agenda — model selection, context length, multilingual, tool calling, security, then next steps. Sound good?
00:00:25 Lena: Yep, that's exactly it.
00:00:30 Maya: Great. To kick off, can you share your primary workloads and success criteria?
00:00:38 Jamal: Sure. Primary---we have a conversational assistant that needs to ingest long conversation histories and docs; typical session can be 15k to 50k tokens, sometimes more. We also need strong non-English support (Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese). Latency SLO for 90% p95 should be ~800ms for short responses, we can tolerate higher for long-context summarization, but cost matters — we have a fixed budget target.
00:01:05 Ravi: Got it. So context length and multilingual are top priorities, plus cost and latency tradeoffs. Are you currently using any models/providers?
00:01:13 Lena: We're prototyping with OpenAI but want to move to an open model stack for economics and control. Interested in dedicated or private deployments for sensitive customers.
00:01:23 Maya: Makes sense. For long context, we typically evaluate both model architecture (some models support 32k natively, a few 64k, some require windowing or chunking) and runtime techniques (KV cache, continuous prefix caching, retrieval augmentation). For Horizon's 50k spikes, we'd look at 64k or higher models or a hybrid where retrieval provides condensed context.
00:01:46 Jamal: Which open models would you recommend for multilingual + long context? We've looked at Llama-2 70B, Mistral-Instruct, MPT-30B, Falcon-180B, and some community 64k variants.
00:02:00 Ravi: High-level: Llama-2 70B quantized can be cost-effective but multilingual can be patchy depending on fine-tune. Mistral has good instruction-tuning but context window depends on variant. MPT and Falcon have community 32k and 65k variants; performance varies. For >=64k tasks we often test: Mistral-64k community builds, GPTQ quantized Llama variants, and newer open models optimized for long context. For best latency/cost we also recommend smaller instruction-tuned models with retrieval, which reduces token cost.
00:02:30 Sofia: On private vs dedicated, question: encryption at rest, KMS, and audit logs — do you provide HSM integrations and tenant-level audit trails?
00:02:39 Maya: Yes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; Dedicated supports server-side encryption and detailed audit logs. We can surface per-request audit events in the Console. We'll send the SOC2 report and KMS docs as part of the security pack.
00:02:56 Lena: Great. For tool calling — we need model-driven function calls for taking actions (e.g., run a search, open a ticket). Does Redwood support structured tool calling with verification?
00:03:08 Ravi: We support streaming responses and function/tool calling primitives. On hosted API we provide native function-calling patterns; for Dedicated/Private we can run the same runtime with function call hooks and webhooks. For safety we can add an action-approval gate or a middleware layer in the console.
00:03:25 Jamal: Is there any limitation around model choices when using function-calling? E.g., can we use community Mistral variants and still have the function-calling layer?
00:03:33 Ravi: Generally yes — function-calling is runtime-level. As long as the model can output structured tokens (JSON-like), our runtime can parse and trigger hooks. Some models are more consistent with structured outputs, so we'd validate during the benchmark.
00:03:45 Lena: Latency: you mentioned batching and quantization. We're worried about p95 spikes with large contexts. How do you manage that?
00:03:53 Ravi: We use continuous batching, dynamic kernel selection, and KV cache-aware batching. For large-context requests we can route to dedicated racks with larger memory or to variants optimized for long context. Also you can configure latency SLOs per route; if p95 can't be met, auto-fallback policy can route to smaller-context summarization model and a retrieval layer, keeping user experience graceful.
00:04:18 Jamal: That fallback sounds useful. For our benchmarks, what would you recommend as a test matrix?
00:04:24 Ravi: I'd propose: 1) Short chat (<=2k tokens) throughput and latency across 3 models, 2) Long-context summarization at 32k and 64k windows, 3) multilingual prompts in Spanish/JP, 4) function-calling reliability tests with instrumentation. We'll capture token-level cost and per-route p50/p95.
00:04:42 Maya: Budget questions — hosted API has fastest time-to-value but per-token costs are higher; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; Private adds compliance overhead but necessary for regulated customers. Is your timeline for a pilot or production?
00:04:55 Lena: We want a pilot in Q4 and production by Q1 next year. Pilot scope is 5k monthly active users with mixed languages.
00:05:04 Maya: Perfectly actionable. Do you have data residency needs?
00:05:08 Sofia: US and EU only, must have options for EU region deployment.
00:05:12 Ravi: We can pin regions in routing policies and provision Dedicated capacity in EU regions. For Private, you manage the infra so residency is controlled by your VPC.
00:05:20 Jamal: A couple of nitty-gritty: tokenization differences between models — how much work is it to switch model families?
00:05:27 Ravi: Tokenization can change effective token counts, especially for non-English. We'll measure tokens per language during the benchmark. Our Optimize tooling suggests quantization and batching profiles per model and per workload to meet cost/latency goals. We'll give you a model-switch impact report.
00:05:41 Lena: Any red flags with using community 64k variants? Stability?
00:05:45 Ravi: Some community builds are bleeding-edge and can have stability or reproducibility issues. For production we prefer Redwood-verified performance profiles — we test model forks and provide recommended variants. If you need cutting-edge 64k, we can run compatibility tests in the pilot.
00:06:00 Sofia: Compliance follow-up — how are logs retained, and can we limit what gets stored?
00:06:05 Maya: Yes — on Dedicated/Private you can configure retention policies; the hosted API has default retention but enterprise plans allow custom retention windows and redaction hooks. We'll include that in the security docs.
00:06:15 Jamal: For function-calling, how do you instrument failures or retries in the runtime? We want traceability from prompt -> function call -> downstream system.
00:06:22 Ravi: The Console has per-request traces showing model output tokens, function call payloads, webhook responses, and retry events. We correlate traces with request IDs, and you can export traces to your observability stack.
00:06:34 Lena: Excellent. Back to models — can you share an initial ranked recommendation for Horizon's needs?
00:06:39 Maya: High level recommendation: 1) For pilot, try a 32k-optimized Llama-2 70B quantized or Mistral instruct to balance cost; 2) For long-context experiments, test a 64k MPT/Falcon variant or community 64k Mistral; 3) Use a retrieval-augmented smaller model for general chat to save tokens; 4) If strict compliance required for specific customers, run Private with verified model artifacts. We'll attach a model comparison table in the follow-up.
00:07:04 Jamal: That sounds good. Any limitations around deployment — e.g., does Private support air-gapped on-prem installs?
00:07:11 Maya: Yes, we have an on-prem package and an air-gapped deployment option. It's more involved engineering-wise; we'd qualify that as part of an enterprise engagement.
00:07:20 Sofia: Can we get an NDA/contract template early? We need to show legal.
00:07:24 Maya: Absolutely, we'll send a presales NDA and enterprise docs with the security pack.
00:07:30 Ravi: Quick question for Jamal — are you open to a benchmark where we run two candidate models in parallel on your prompts to compare p95 and cost per effective token?
00:07:38 Jamal: Yes, that's exactly what we want.
00:07:41 Maya: Great. Anything else?
00:07:44 Lena: Just one more: internationalization — do you support model-specific tokenizers and can you provide per-language evaluation metrics?
00:07:51 Ravi: We do. We'll include per-language BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics and qualitative examples in the benchmark report.
00:07:58 Sofia: And one more security ask: can we have an architecture diagram of Dedicated in EU region with KMS flow?
00:08:05 Maya: We'll include that in the pack.
00:08:08 Maya: Okay let's recap next steps...
00:08:12 Maya: We'll send pricing and model comparison, security pack with SOC2/KMS/HSM info and CDN/region details, schedule the technical deep-dive for two weeks out, and Ravi will propose benchmark plan.
00:08:22 Lena: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
00:08:25 Jamal: Thanks.
00:08:27 Sofia: Thanks.
00:08:30 Maya: End call.
